subject: Azure private offer: hourly vs reserved SKU — channel margin pass-through
messages:
From: Patricia Gomez <pgomez@cloudhealth.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cloudhealth.io
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer for Azure — hourly + reserved mix, channel margin question

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — CloudHealth is ready to move forward for a pilot in Q3. Procurement asked me to capture the pricing shape so we can loop in our reseller (PartnerEdge) and finalize PO timing. Two implementation notes:

- We expect 60% of spend to be steady-state (monthly predictable) and want reserved-instance pricing for that portion.
- The other ~40% will be spiky/hourly. We prefer a single private offer that covers both SKUs if possible.

Key ask: PartnerEdge needs confirmation of the channel margin pass-through in the private offer. They historically require a visible reseller margin on the invoice (or an agreed rebate mechanism). Can you confirm how Redwood represents channel splits on Azure private offers and what options we have for showing/allocating margin for PartnerEdge?

I've attached a short doc with our expected consumption mix and procurement timeline. Ideally we need a signed PO by Aug 8.

Thanks —
Patricia Gomez
Head of Cloud Economics, CloudHealth Analytics
pgomez@cloudhealth.io

Attachment: cloudhealth_private_offer_request.docx (docx)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Patricia Gomez <pgomez@cloudhealth.io>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer for Azure — hourly + reserved mix, channel margin question

Patricia — thanks, this is clear and reasonable. Looping in Vanessa (channels) and Ben (pricing ops) to propose two pragmatic ways to structure the private offer so PartnerEdge sees their margin. High level options:

1) "Invoice-visible" pass-through: create the private offer with list-price and a reseller line item (PartnerEdge) with a fixed percentage pass-through. Azure will surface the reseller fee on the invoice. This is the cleanest for PartnerEdge’s accounting but requires us to accept a slightly wider gross-to-net spread.

2) "Rebate-backed" channel margin: Redwood issues the private offer at net pricing (lower list), and we record a separate reseller rebate SOW that gets paid out monthly/quarterly to PartnerEdge. This keeps the private offer tidy on Azure but adds an off-invoice settlement step.

Practical considerations for CloudHealth:
- If you need the margin visible for audits, option 1 is recommended.
- If you prefer simpler billing and accept an SOW for the reseller, option 2 reduces immediate list-price impact.

Ben/Vanessa — can you confirm the typical band we can offer for an enterprise pilot: visible pass-through percent vs rebate percent? Patricia — we'll aim to draft both variants and send a single private-offer bundle you can sign.

Next steps: I can circulate a short draft private offer (Azure format) with both variants by end of day tomorrow. If Aug 8 PO is the target we'll need the reseller acceptance within 5 business days of that draft.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Quick internal note and recommended margin structures (for Ben/Karthik to review before we send drafts):

Option A (Invoice-visible pass-through):
- Reseller line item: 9% of gross list for pilot (typical for PartnerEdge where they do full resale + managed services).
- We will show two SKUs: AZ-RESERVED (60% volume) + AZ-HOURLY (40% volume). Reseller fee line applies to total consumption.
- Pros: PartnerEdge sees margin on invoice; clean for their finance team.
- Cons: Slightly higher list -> potential customer sticker shock.

Option B (Off-invoice rebate):
- Net list discount to CloudHealth ~7% off our public private-offer list; separate monthly rebate to PartnerEdge equal to 9% of gross.
- Pros: Cleaner invoice for CloudHealth; easier for Redwood gross-to-net handling.
- Cons: PartnerEdge must accept rebate cadence and SOW.

Operational asks:
- Ben: confirm Azure private-offer template supports explicit reseller line item and sample payload we should feed to marketplace.
- Karthik: can we include an explicit 'reserved coverage' split inside the single private-offer bundle? Azure allows multiple SKUs in one offer but we should test the billing path.

I'll draft both variants and mark each with the expected accounting treatment. Patricia — copying PartnerEdge so they can confirm the margin tolerance.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Channel GTM, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

- An estimated blended rate (hourly/reserved) for the pilot so procurement can size the PO.
- A DocuSign link or simplified acceptance method — procurement prefers signed private-offer PDF + PO.

Patricia Gomez
